STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style plate with cooked bacon strips and cut melon cubes (cantaloupe and honeydew-style pale green melon). Photographed from directly above, so the plate is seen nearly undistorted.

STEP 2 - Ruler: Pale blue plate, roughly 26 cm in diameter (dinner-plate size). Area = 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: (1) bacon, about 3 strips, cooked; (2) orange cantaloupe cubes; (3) pale green honeydew cubes.

STEP 4 - Area:
- Bacon: about 12% of plate area (~64 cm²)
- Orange melon cubes: about 14% (~74 cm²)
- Green melon cubes: about 15% (~80 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 41% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (height estimates from visible piece sizes, roughly 2 to 2.5 cm cubes and thin bacon):
- Bacon: 64 cm² x 0.4 cm ≈ 26 ml
- Orange melon: 74 cm² x 2 cm ≈ 148 ml
- Green melon: 80 cm² x 2 cm ≈ 160 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Bacon: 26 ml x 0.9 ≈ 23 g
- Orange melon: 148 ml x 0.6 ≈ 89 g
- Green melon: 160 ml x 0.6 ≈ 96 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Bacon (cooked): 23 g x 540 kcal/100g ≈ 124 kcal
- Cantaloupe: 89 g x 34 kcal/100g ≈ 30 kcal
- Honeydew: 96 g x 36 kcal/100g ≈ 35 kcal
Total ≈ 208 kcal, about 208 g.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 200 g of food with roughly 200 kcal fits a light breakfast of three bacon strips and a bowl-sized portion of melon on a plate that is only partly covered. Plausible.

Estimated total: about 208 g, about 190–210 kcal.
